text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered — GPU queue growth for customer-prod-vpc-12 (customer: AcmeHealth).
incident-bot: metric: gpu_queue_length=124, scale_attempts=3, last_scale_error="node-provision-timeout". dashboard: https://infra.redwood/d/queues/customer-prod-vpc-12

sara: acked. i'm oncall. assigning triage. anyone on gpu-provisioning?

mike: i'm grabbing the autoscaler logs now. likely provisioning timeouts from bootstrapping step. will paste logs in a sec.

junaid: seeing similar in logs: "Provisioner: launch instances failed: quota or capacity error". region us-west-2 reported spare GPU capacity=0 for preferred instance types.

ops-liz: customer cluster has strict nodeSelector/taints to only allow p4d instance type. that pool shows 0 available due to infra maintenance earlier.

mike: log excerpt:
```
E0321 14:05:22.123 12345 provisioner.go:142] failed to start node: timeout waiting for kubelet registration
E0321 14:06:03.456 12345 cloudprovider.go:88] LaunchInstances error: InsufficientInstanceCapacity: We currently do not have sufficient capacity for the requested instance type.
```

emma-cs: customer on support line — they report 30% of inference requests are queued >2s and some timeouts. flagged as customer impact.

sara: assessing blast radius: only AcmeHealth cluster (private VPC) is impacted. Hosted fallback not enabled for this customer. need mitigation quick.

junaid: immediate mitigations we can try:
- relax nodeSelector/taints for the pool to allow alternative GPU types (p3 -> p4), if customer config permits
- temporarily allow burst to shared dedicated pool in us-west-2 (requires infra approval)
- re-route low-priority traffic to fallback hosted models if possible

mike: i'm going to attempt a conservative change: add toleration for p3-like nodes and request autoscaler to try again. will post command.

mike: running:
```
kubectl -n acme apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: gpu-toleration-prep
spec:
  tolerations:
  - key: "gpu-type"
    operator: "Exists"
EOF
```

ops-liz: i can open a burst-capacity request but that takes ~8-12min. i'm starting it now. ticket -> #infra-burst-3872.

deploy-bot: Automatic rollouts to customer-prod-vpc-12 have been paused due to high queue lengths.

mike: autoscaler log after toleration change: "scale attempt 4 -> started; requested 2 nodes; launch in progress". pushing watch.

incident-bot: update: queue=98 (was 124) after partial scale.

emma-cs: letting customer know we're mitigating and ETA ~15-30m. sending standard incident note.

sara: good. status call in 10. if scale fails again we need to failover traffic at the nginx layer to hosted fallback and open a sev ticket with account execs.

(10m later)

mike: partial success — 1 node registered. another launch still failing with InsufficientInstanceCapacity for p4a. logs show image pull delays on node bootstrap as well (registry throttle).

ops-liz: registry spikes due to concurrent private cluster boots earlier. i'm increasing parallel pulls throttle and retry window.

junaid: note: autoscaler hit max_nodes limit for that pool (max=8, current=8). that's why scale attempts kept failing earlier. we should increase max_nodes as emergency step.

sara: increasing max_nodes to 12 for pool acme-prod-pool. mike, can you validate no cost policy blockers? this is emergency.

mike: increasing now via infra API. command: `infractl pools update acme-prod-pool --max-nodes 12`

incident-bot: action logged by sara (oncall): increased pool max from 8->12.

mike: second node registered. queue=56. timeouts still happening for long requests, but tail latency improving.

emma-cs: customer updated: "we see improvement, thanks — still some retries but service recovering."

sara: postmortem notes so far: root causes suspected = (1) constrained instance type + region capacity, (2) pool max_nodes too low for traffic spike, (3) image registry throttles slowed node bootstrap.

mike: next steps for recovery:
- keep pool at 12 until traffic normalizes and then rollback to pre-incident config with approval
- add fallback routing option to allow hosted model fallback for private customers (ops/security approval needed)
- add autoscaler alert when scale_attempts>2 and pool at max_nodes

ops-liz: opened infra ticket with cloud provider about instance capacity, and registry team ticket for pull-rate adjustments. ids: CP-542, REG-119.

sara: handing off to night oncall: @mike you own until handoff in 30m, after that @junaid-night takes over. create an incident ticket in PagerDuty linking this thread.

mike: created PD incident PD-INC-89321, linked. adding runbook entry for temp max_nodes increase.

emma-cs: CS notified account exec and logged customer impact in CRM.

deploy-bot: Reminder: automatic rollouts remain paused for affected service until a post-incident review.

sara: summary for post-incident: immediate mitigations applied (tolerations, raised pool max, burst request, registry throttle adjustments). customer impact limited to queued requests and elevated tail latency for ~40m. follow-ups: add autoscaler guardrails, provide customer a formal incident note, review pool sizing defaults for private VPCs.

sara: closing live thread. will reopen if regressions occur. :white_check_mark:
